description: Sync a catalogue of the files in the Figma projects you choose: each file's name, project, last modified time and link. Design content is not synced.
opening: Sync a catalogue of the files in the Figma projects you select. Each file is one document holding its name, project, last modified time and link, so a search can find a file by name and take you to it.

Design content is not read: frames, text layers, components and comments are not synced. Figma permissions are not imported, so every synced file is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. The first sync lists only files modified in the last 30 days unless you raise `lookback_days`. Files deleted in Figma stay in HydraDB.

connect.text: HydraDB needs your Figma team ids to list your projects, because Figma's API cannot list a user's teams. The connection form does not ask for them yet, which is why Figma is in beta.

connect.auth: Figma uses a personal access token.

steps.title: Create a personal access token
steps.text: In Figma, create a personal access token for a user who can see the projects you want catalogued.

steps.title: Select projects
steps.text: HydraDB lists the projects of your Figma teams. Select the projects to sync. To reach files older than 30 days, raise `lookback_days` when you select them.

connect.account: One connector reads what one Figma user's token can see.

sync.first_sync: Each selected project reads back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default. Files last modified before that window are not listed.
sync.changes: Each sync lists the files modified since the last sync.
sync.edits: A file whose last modified time moved is sent again with its new details.
sync.deletes: Deleted files are not removed. A file deleted in Figma stays searchable in HydraDB.

documents.name: Files
documents.one_document: One Figma file's details. Its design content is not included.
documents.title: The file name. A file with no name is titled `Figma file` and its key.
documents.text: The title, then `Project`, `Last modified` and `Link` lines. This is the only searchable text for a file.
documents.date: When the file was last modified.

attributes.name: project_name
attributes.text: The project name, written as the `Project` line when HydraDB has it. The name is often missing, so to limit a query to a project, use `additional_metadata.figma_project_id`.

attributes.name: last_modified
attributes.text: When the file was last modified, written as the `Last modified` line. Sets the result date.

attributes.name: url
attributes.text: The Figma link built from the file key, written as the `Link` line.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.figma_project_id
attributes.text: The id of the project that holds the file. Limits a query to one project's files. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.figma_file_key
attributes.text: The file key. Picks out one file. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's files. Not searchable.

attributes.name: thumbnail_url
attributes.text: The address of the file's thumbnail image, for your own app to show. HydraDB does not read the image.

example_searches: Is there a Figma file for the checkout redesign?
Which files in this Figma project changed recently?
What is the link to the onboarding flow design?

connections: No links between files, and no links to items in other tools.
graph.from_text: The file name and, when present, the project name. There is no design content to read.

not_synced: Files last modified before the `lookback_days` window on the first sync.
Design content: frames, text layers and components.
Thumbnail images. Only their address is kept.
Deletions: deleted files stay in HydraDB.
